gaps: No visually inspected inscription image was available in this research, so the reported bronze and manuscript glyph readings were not independently checked from the artifacts or facsimiles.

The inscription compilation reports a Spring and Autumn bronze form with 言+可 and later 欠+哥 forms, but the transition and component-by-component lineage are not proven by the opened sources. Do not assign a definite earlier_form or full_form relation to components solely from these different reported shapes; use uncertain when a distinct origin_form requires classification.

Shuowen directly supports 欠 as the semantic classifier and 哥 as sound in its analyzed form. Whether the early 言+可 bronze graph is an earlier form of the later 欠+哥 graph, a graphic variant, or a related spelling needs specialist paleographic corroboration.

The standalone 哥 component has Mandarin gē and is grouped with 歌 at Zhengzhang *kaːl in the inspected comparison table. Equivalent same-system Baxter–Sagart data for 哥 was not established in the inspected page; avoid implying the two reconstructions are identical across systems.

The poem 《園有桃》 is cited by dictionaries for early use of 歌 as singing, but the reviewed sources did not establish the poem’s composition date or the date of a physical manuscript bearing the graph. Earliest secure graph attestation and earliest word use remain unresolved.
Later senses (praise, musical piece, verse genre, bell name) are attested in cited classical texts, but no source consulted established when or by what semantic steps these senses developed.

The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison with Burmese ka ‘dance’ was not independently verified through a primary comparative source or early Burmese attestations; keep it separate from character graphic history and label it uncertain.
No evidence supports a graph-loan analysis for 歌 in this research. The Shuowen note that 哥 could write 謌/歌 is relevant to graph usage, but is not proof that 歌 itself originated as a whole-graph loan.
The late Spring-and-Autumn bronze and Warring States forms are reported by a secondary collation; their artifact images and readings were not independently checked against primary facsimiles.

The relation between the reported early 言+可 structure and the received 欠+哥 form remains uncertain. It could reflect chronological change, a variant spelling, or a related form; the available evidence does not justify choosing among these.
The earliest secure physical attestation of 歌 and the date of a surviving witness to its early textual use remain unresolved. Shijing citations do not by themselves date the extant written graph.
The citation sequence does not establish the semantic chronology or pathways for singing, song, praise, and verse-genre senses.

The possible Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison with Burmese ka ‘dance’ was not independently verified with a primary comparative source or dated Burmese evidence; it is separate from the graph’s formation.

No whole-graph borrowing account for 歌 is supported by the inspected sources. Shuowen’s note that 哥 could be used to write 謌/歌 concerns spelling practice and does not prove the origin of 歌 as a graph loan.
The Xiaoxuetang page could be opened, and its guide confirmed the official CC0 notice, but this browser did not expose its form labels or images. No Xiaoxuetang candidate was selected.
No direct reusable image of the reported bronze inscription was established, so the selected Commons candidate is a modern redraw of the received Shuowen seal form, not an ancient artifact image.

The Commons file description search result names 歌-seal.svg but the description page and direct file endpoints could not be opened in this invocation. The prior packet's acquisition finding reports a 404 for its candidate direct image URL. Since an actual working direct image URL could not be verified, no glyph image is selected.

The early 言+可 and received 欠+哥 forms are reported in a secondary collation. Their chronological relationship, component ancestry, and whether they are variants or related spellings remain unresolved; the artifact/facsimile pixels were not independently checked.

The Shijing citation supports an early textual use claim in reference works, but no date of composition or surviving written witness was established here. Earliest secure physical attestation remains unresolved.
The consulted sources do not establish a chronology or pathway among singing, song, praise, and poetic-genre senses. No whole-graph borrowing account is established.
No primary inscription image or facsimile was inspected. The reported bronze example is secondary evidence only, and sources disagree on its bronze catalogue number (集成184 versus 集成186).

The transition or relationship between reported early 言+可 and received 欠+哥 is unresolved: chronology, variant status, regional spelling, and possible graphic corruption were not decided by the inspected sources. Do not assign origin_form ancestry from these reports alone.
Shuowen supports a semantic-classifier role for 欠 and phonetic role for 哥 in the received form; the text does not establish that this analysis applies to the earliest reported spelling.

The Shijing citation supports textual use of 歌 as ‘sing,’ but no inspected evidence dates the physical witness bearing that graph. No chronology or pathway among sing, song, praise, verse genre and the cited bell name was established.

The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows report 歌 *[k]ˤaj and 欠 *[k]ʰ(r)om-s; no supplied row gives 哥 in that system, so no Baxter–Sagart component-host comparison can be reported. Zhengzhang provides the same-system match 歌/哥 *kaːl.
Current Mandarin local rows are available for 歌 gē, 哥 gē and 欠 qiàn, but official Unicode Unihan character pages could not be inspected in this pass; URLs were attempted and returned internal errors.
The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison with Burmese ka remains unverified through independent comparative or dated Burmese evidence and is separate from graphic formation.
No whole-graph borrowing origin for 歌 is supported. Shuowen’s note concerning spelling with 哥/謌 does not demonstrate that 歌 originated as a whole-character loan.
